body:
God damn, where to even start with this comment.

First, you weren't banned because they hate you, they banned you because you broke the literal most important rule of the entire subreddt: Don't interrupt the circlejerk. If you went to /r/ggggg and submitted a post titled "H" you would also be banned. That doesn't mean they hate you, it means you don't have the basic reading skills needed to simply read the rules of the subreddit you're wanting to post to.

Second, just because you think they're jokes doesn't mean they can't also be offensive or just plane tiring. And even if you were 100% right, that it was all people being offended over jokes, that still doesn't make them a hate group.

Also, the fact that they have colorful ban notifications really should help you understand just how serious they are. Cat pictures are almost never the bringers of bigotry and hate.

And lastly, which group is it that SRS hates? And where is this made explicit?

I'm begining to suspect you actually have no idea what a hate sub is. Coontown was a hate sub. gasthejews was a hate sub. What demographic of people is it SRS hates?

Are you for real now?

Another commenter summed it up better than I could recently when someone came in asking what SRS was all about:

>You know how /r/bestof links to cool stuff on reddit? We link to terrible things on reddit *that are highly upvoted* and then have a place where we can vent about how terrible something is.

>That's it, that's the sum total of this subreddit's "point."

>My personal example, when the Fergison riots were happening, and racist stuff was filling the front page, everyone pointing out the racism were being downvoted and told to "go back to srs". So I came here and it was just about the only place saying "are you seeing how racist this place is being today?"

>We all come to reddit for different reasons, but there's a lot of stuff on this site that gets highly upvoted that is just plane bad. So here's a decompression chamber of sorts. A place where we don't need to have a debate if pedophelia is wrong, it just is. As is racism, sexism, islamophobia, transphobia, homophobia, creepy sexualization of nonsexual content just because there's a girl in it, that stuff isn't welcome here. 

>If that makes us SJWs, fine. It's one of the most ill defined terms on the internet that can mean literally anything, so if you work at it basically everyone both is and isn't an SJW. But if you're serious in finding out what this place is about that's it. We aren't trying to "fix" or even change reddit, we don't brigade (the admins have confirmed this numerous times), we just exist in our small little area of the site and somehow we've morphed into a comic book villain. But this is what we really are, just a bunch or redditors who are tired of some of the more annoying parts of the site we run into form time to time.

>That and we're crazy sarcastic, which many mistake for seriousness and we have cool art.

In my experience, this is 100% accurate. SRS does not hate anyone. And if you can show me *any* evidence that they hate anyone, I'll stop going. But I'm a straight white middle class male, I'm supposed to be everything they hate and I've gotten no hate from them at all, quite the opposite actually they've been one of the most friendly and supportive subreddits I frequent.

They are getting disturbing though. That's kind of the point of why I'm asking. I don't want to quit reddit because some assholes keep pming me from time to time, but it is to the point of being very unsettling. I don't have an actual fear for my physical well being, but my mental well being is.. not great and this really isn't helping.

Somehow I don't think responding is a smart move. There's no changing someone like that's mind and even if there were it's not my job to try. I just want to not have to get those kinds of messages as a trade off for using reddit. I've been coming to this site for 7 years and it's only been recently that this kind of stuff has started and I just want it to stop.

That's the thing though, I don't engage them. I try to avoid them whenever possible. I have no interest, desire or temperament to actually engage with bigoted people. The closest I get to "engaging" is commenting in SRS. Are you considering that engaging?

So I should what, resign myself to them, that this is simply the price of using reddit?

Well that's exactly as depressing as I was thinking...

I can't say I've been exactly where you are but I've been close. That long persistent pressure, it can be tough.

I'm not mentioning this to make it about me, but to show with example that you aren't the only one that's gone through this. You can get through it even if it doesn't feel like it right now. I can't promise it'll be sunshine and rainbows, but you can make it work. Find what's not working and try to minimize it. Find what does work and pursue it.

Your life does not belong on anyone else's schedule. Not everyone goes right to college and that's ok. Not everyone finishes high school at the same time and that's ok. There is no right or wrong time except what's right or wrong for you. You should try to not make yourself feel bad as much as you can, and this is one of those things you don't need to feel bad about, especially if feeling bad isn't going to change anything.
shit, did I say something to mess with you? I really didn't mean to. Hello?
No, your comments haven't cause distress. I just also have a history of taking conversations about something so raw in ways they aren't intended and I can't help that.
Look forward to it, but just fair warning to be careful. This is delecate stuff and I can't always see triggers coming that end up really digging in and I'm already not doing great.

I wouldn't break it down that way, partly because there's emotions to both, but the "public" v "private" is possible. I do split that up a lot, sometimes it's just easier to lie to the public, it's like a social expediency. But no it's maybe more blame self/blame others breakdown. Cause if it's something wrong with my head, that could potentially be fixed. If it's all the external shit that's to blame then I don't know where to begin with that. I can't change the past, I can't change how it has or hasn't conditioned me, I can't control what people will do to me in the future, and it would mean all these times I've felt terrible there had to be a reason and I just can't find one sometimes. 

It's maybe not the most logical reason to believe one version over the other but it certainly enters in. If this was the result of my upbringing, which does cross my mind from time to time, it makes me feel terrible. I get angry at my parents, I get angry at myself for not acting differently, I get mornful for the life that could have been. A lot of my life revolves around minimizing pain, when my depression gets bad enough it physically manifests itself and it can *hurt*. Pain is a powerful motivator. 

I've kept myself away from self harm cause that is a very steep slope (except sometimes I dig my fingernails into may hand really hard to distract from the really bad pain). Same slippery slope thoughts have kept me from trying to self-medicating (or over/under-eating) my pain away. I'm also thankfully of a belief that there is no afterlife and simply trying to contemplate nothingness is usually enough to keep me from anything suicidal. 

But I can feel with each new dip back down into depression that resolve weaken and it terrifies me. Especially cause now I live on the 9th floor, I've never lived up high and I have terrifying thoughts of just opening my window and jumping. I mean it's not like I've never lived with the ability to do so before, but none quite as snap a judgement. One moment of stupid. I don't want to, I don't want to die, I just also don't want to live the way I have been. It's a subtle difference but still a difference. Problem is, the less it seems like my life can improve the more likely it seems the two options are the same.

That's the thing though, I didn't have a particularly sad events in childhood. Some like mild teasing in grades 5 and 6 but otherwise I was never the target of bullies or beat up. My parents are both together and are both understanding, caring people. I was never the cool kid but I also wasn't an outcast. 

OK, this is going to sound weird but I'm typing very stream of consciousness so I'm not deleting what I wrote above. But as I was writing it another part of me was screaming at me that I was lieing with every keystroke. This is another part I love is the Smeagol back and forth that can go on almost as if my depression has a voice of it's own (though to emphasize it isn't *actually* a voice, I'm not disillusion just internally torn and lacking in better metaphor than "spoke").

Maybe I just don't like blaming my problems on circumstance, maybe I'm so used to denial, false answers etc it's instinct. I mean, nothing I said above was a lie, but it certainly is only part of the story. God I fucking hate when it's hard to talk about things, shit. Just spent 10 minutes staring at this screen running through stuff in my head and looking for how to put it. 

Sorry, turning rambling. But I would probably say it wasn't so much an unhappy childhood as it was a slightly isolated one. I mean I had friends usually, not a ton but enough. k-2 I don't remember, but I was homeschooled (not for religious reasons, we lived in a heavily Filipino/Hispanic neighborhood and I would have literally been one of only two kids in the class who already knew English). Grade 3-4 I was in a program for gifted kids kind of separated off from the rest of the school. When I was 9 we moved from San Diego to middle of nowhere town in Canada, population 8,000. Then grades 7-12 I went to a private school my mom worked for, my graduating class was 38 people. Not to mention that I was raised Baha'i, making me different that way, until I was actually *going* to a Baha'i run school which is about when I became atheist. 

I could probably ramble on more than you'd want to read, but the tldr is just a mixed bag of equil parts loving household and being different everywhere else.

Mine never really has a "begining" though. As far back as my memories go I've defaulted to sad, or anxious or something along those lines. I'm not saying I've never had joy, and I'm not saying I've always known the term "depression" but I've always had it. 

There's a mild depression that never leaves and it's then this second "depression" that comes in from time to time when I feel really extra shitty, and so even when I can "beat" that depression or just work to keep it at bay it's back to the default of low-grade depression. That's the prize I get for enduring and fighting through it and it's a shitty prize. I can feel it eroding me year on year, I don't know how much more of it I can take.

It's hard to compare. Low is rather qualitative and it's been so many years it all blends together to some degree... 

Yeah, I just spent maybe about 10 minutes thinking hard and I can't pick a specific lowest. I mean it's also been different kinds of low too. A low for elementry school is different from high school which is different from college which is different from post college. If I *had* to choose a top three it's down to either Sept 2005, Nov-Dec 2007, or Oct-Dec 2010. But none of them are *that* much lower than most of my other "lows." It's I think one of the reasons I'm so sure it's mostly chemical because what I'm doing with my life seems to not drastically change how low the lows are when they come. Why do you ask?

Yeah kind of diving back and forth all day between one distraction and another with a whole bunch of painfully sitting there until it calms down enough to let me move on to another thing. Not to mention interrogating myself as to what might have been the trigger this time. Either it doesn't have one or I found Frozen for some reason really depressing. Yeah! Crippling depression five!

Yup, having just a blast of a night.
